definitions.note: used here as a noun: British slang for a decrepit old car

indicators.note: a bird eating something has it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a jay is a bird, a flier
to lop is to chop off

explanation.surface: A bird tucks into a pork chop and a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests a sausage beside the chop, but here it is British slang for a clapped-out car.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a battered, worn-out old motor car.

clue.text: Summit meeting of psychologist and wife

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychologist
Frau is German for wife

explanation.surface: A summit conference between a psychologist and a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit meeting' suggests talks between leaders, but 'Summit' is a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a famous mountain peak in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Floor covering, kind that's used by printers

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: something printers use

parts.note: lino is short for linoleum, a floor covering
a type is a kind

explanation.surface: A sort of floor covering that printers use.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a typesetting machine casting whole lines of metal type, long used in newspaper printing.

definitions.meaning: a nobleman, member of the House of Lords
to gaze closely, squint

explanation.definitionFit: A noble with a seat in the Lords; and the verb for peering closely at something.

clue.text: Old boy, wearing sulky expression, ceased to be involved

indicators.note: a pout wearing a boy has him on the inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pout is a sulky look
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A former pupil, pulling a sulky face, has stopped taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' looks like one phrase for a former pupil, but splits into O and the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To have chosen to withdraw from something is to have stopped being involved in it.

parts.note: suggests bunting hung over a street, but flags are also flat slabs of stone

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of flags waving in a street party; the flags meant are flagstones underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are the slabs used to surface pavements.

clue.text: One is belted and real aggravated

indicators.note: made worse, roughed up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone gets a belting and is genuinely angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belted' suggests a beating, but an earl is invested with a sword-belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman of this rank was traditionally girded with a belt on being created.

clue.text: It's hateful having nothing and five hundred debts

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
D is the Roman numeral for 500
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Having no money and a lot of debts is a hateful position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something detestable, deserving loathing.

parts.note: suggests a driving lesson or a racetrack, but means a golfer's first drive at a hole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' and 'course' suggest a car on a track; in golf you drive from the tee on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers begin each hole by striking the ball from a peg on the teeing ground.

clue.text: Grandma gets setback in French city

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for grandmother

indicators.note: the word set is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grandmother suffers a setback while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' reads as one word, but splits into SET and the reversal signal 'back', making TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a major city in western France, on the Loire.

definitions.note: used as a verb: to strain or exhaust

parts.note: overt means open, done publicly
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A levy that provokes outrage among the populace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a noun (a levy) but is the verb meaning to strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to strain their strength, which is to exhaust them too much.

clue.text: Answered call instantly but was pipped at the post?

definitions.meaning: entered at once when summoned, in a moment
finished runner-up in a race, beaten narrowly at the line

explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'came in a second' it means arrived very quickly; read as a finishing position it means runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving in a moment when called, or finishing behind the winner in a race.

clue.text: A couple of notes and that's your lot!

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
te is another note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A teacher gives two more notes and says that is all you get.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny, what fortune has allotted.

definitions.meaning: a ... colour is pale, washed out
to lose consciousness, swoon

explanation.surface: Someone turns white and collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale colour is a faint one; to pass out is to swoon, lose consciousness.

clue.text: Belt as part of a shirt

definitions.meaning: to belt is to strike, hit
the band at the end of a sleeve

explanation.surface: A belt worn as some part of a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to strike them; the band round the wrist of a shirt sleeve has the same name.

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up a word reverses it

parts.note: met, as in met a target
PI, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: Feeling uplifted, someone has had some very good times.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for very good is a crossword convention from pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, a musical speed or pace.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Waves seen out at sea from a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' suggests ocean waves, but means posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells and toffs are both British slang for fashionable upper-class people.

definitions.meaning: grasp, comprehension of something
anxiety about what may happen

explanation.surface: Comprehension that one ought to be afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both grasping something mentally and dreading what is to come.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another puts it first

parts.note: to side with someone is to be partial to them
rum is British informal for odd, unusual

explanation.surface: Someone was fond of an unusual instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places SIDED above RUM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum, a small drum played with sticks, is also called this.

clue.text: Surprised to see first part was first

parts.note: the start is the first part of something
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find the opening section came first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken aback, jumping in shock, is to be surprised.

clue.text: Yet it could be close combat

definitions.text: Yet it could be close combat

parts.words: Yet it could be close combat
parts.note: close combat suggests hand-to-hand fighting; the joke is that close is the opposite of open, yet the fighting can be both

explanation.walkthrough: Close is the opposite of open, hence 'Yet'; but warfare waged in the open can still be fought at close quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Undisguised fighting or hostility, which may well be hand-to-hand combat.

clue.text: Sort of arrangement that's free for all

indicators.note: free signals the letters of the words are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of arrangement open to everyone, a free-for-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free for all' reads as a phrase meaning a chaotic scramble; 'free' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower arrangement is the kind described by this adjective, meaning made of flowers.

clue.text: One may play it — and one may get licked

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument like a small trumpet
a cone holding ice cream

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a brass instrument for playing and, in Britain, an ice-cream cone for licking.

clue.text: Great many will embrace love or money

indicators.note: embracing something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a lot is a great many
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Plenty of people will choose love over riches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the phrase 'for love or money'; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is slang for money, originally plunder.

parts.note: read as 'we in fer', the letters WE placed inside FER

explanation.surface: Someone concludes there are not many of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infer' must be split into 'in' and 'fer': WE inside FER spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smaller number means not so many; the comparative of few.

definitions.meaning: a judge tries a case, sitting in court to examine it
to perceive speech with the ears

explanation.definitionFit: A judge tries a case, which is also called listening to it; and to catch speech is to take it in by ear.

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play
a mould, or the shape made from one

explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a production; and a mould, or a shape made in one.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
ash is waste left after burning

explanation.surface: Plenty of people turn down instant payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' reads as a verb, but is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins in hand are ready money.

clue.text: Goes crazy — manages satisfactorily after a minute

indicators.note: the satisfactory part comes after the minute, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
OK means satisfactorily

explanation.surface: Someone flips out after a minute of things going well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manages satisfactorily' looks like one phrase, but its two words go either side of A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave wildly and uncontrollably is to lose one's head, go berserk.

definitions.meaning: an evergreen bush such as the bay
of the comedy duo ... and Hardy, the one who is not Hardy

explanation.surface: A gardener says the shrub is perennial but not hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the gardening term for frost-resistant, but it is Oliver Hardy, partner of Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay is an evergreen bush of that family; Stan of that name was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner.

definitions.meaning: freedom of action, leeway
a parallel on a map measuring distance north or south of the equator

explanation.surface: Permission granted for a mapmaker's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means leeway or freedom, and also a map parallel north or south of the equator.

parts.note: suggests a child playing, but means the two words sound alike at the end

explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites us to picture a child at play, but it is about the words: boy and toy end in the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words with matching end sounds, like boy and toy, are said to have this relation in verse.
